svg.title: Cross-sector TP convergence and divergence by tacit knowledge type
svg.desc: Ten tacit knowledge types are arranged as wedges. Three concentric layers show Construction, Manufacturing, and Health Services coverage. Marker and callout colors identify the relational, somatic, or collective retention taxonomy, while outside panels list convergent and divergent technology-enabled retention practice relationships.

g.text: Cross-sector Distribution of Tacit Knowledge Retained
Sector layers show TK coverage; callouts distinguish TP relationships recurring across sectors from those identified in only one sector.
TP01; TP04; TP06; TP07; TP13; TP16
Embodied Posture, Balance, and Spatial Control
Immediate Embodied Response to Changing Conditions
Knowledge Conveyed Through Examples or Demonstration
Organizational Culture and Unwritten Working Practices
Informal Coordination, Communication, and Escalation Know-how
Shared Professional Norms and Standards of Judgment
TP01; TP04; TP09; TP10; TP11; TP12
Shared Professional Language and Contextual Meaning
Interpretive rule. TP convergence means the same TP–TK relationship appears in at least two sectors; TP divergence means it appears in only one sector.
“None identified” and uncolored sector cells refer only to the selected evidence and do not establish absence.
Inner: Construction · Middle: Manufacturing · Outer: Health Services
